controller_types.description: Controller-to-engine frame types (spec §25.6 handshake + §25.7). Documented-open: an unsupported type produces a protocol.error, it is not rejected by the envelope (API-009).

engine_types.description: Engine-to-controller frame types (spec §25.6 handshake + §25.8). Documented-open: an unsupported type produces a protocol.error, it is not rejected by the envelope (API-009).

tool_call.description: A tool the model asked to run, as it crosses the engine boundary. The provider emits arguments as a JSON string; the controller resolves it to an object exactly once before the frame is built, so the engine only ever sees an object (spec §25.9).

id.description: The provider's tool_call id (E12 T1b); optional and additive — deterministic fakes and pre-T1b checkpoints may omit it. Recorded verbatim on the assistant turn so the engine can translate the synthetic tcall_ id to it when writing the tool result to the provider conversation. The synthetic tcall_ id still keys the tool.request/tool.result frames and the platform ledger.

messages.description: Prior-response conversation history the engine folds in before input (spec §9, §22.2). The controller assembles it from the session's earlier responses; a purged response is carried as a redacted_content marker, and a first response omits it.

output_contract.description: The run's OUTPUT CONTRACT (spec §22.7), absent when the request named no format — which is every run that does not opt in. The controller resolves it at admission and ALSO applies it itself: it renders the schema as the provider's own decoding constraint on every model request of the run, and it validates the final answer before the response may be called completed. The engine is given it because the engine owns the loop and the terminal frame — it is the only participant that can end a run failed with schema_validation_failed at the boundary where the answer is produced, and the only one that could later spend a bounded repair step on it (§22.7). The controller's own validation is NOT redundant with the engine's: `engine` is a caller-selectable request field, so a third-party engine that ignores this object must still be unable to produce a completed run whose output violates the caller's schema.

format.description: Only json_schema reaches the engine; a text contract demands nothing and the field is omitted entirely.

name.description: The schema's name, forwarded to providers that require one.

schema.description: The JSON Schema 2020-12 document the final output must satisfy.

strict.description: Whether the provider was asked to CONSTRAIN decoding rather than merely be instructed by the schema. Server-side validation runs either way.

workspace_mode.description: The workspace a delegated child receives (spec §29.8, §30.5): none = no workspace (the E08 default); read_only = a read-only snapshot of the parent's; isolated = an isolated copy-on-write branch/worktree. The value is declared here in E09 Task 1 (schema-pin) and enforced in Task 6; before E09 it rode the frame Go/Py-only.

remote_agent.description: A REGISTERED remote A2A agent (an a2a_remote_agents id, spec §38.5) that executes this delegation instead of a local engine (E19 Task 5). Present only when the delegation names one, so a local delegation's frame is byte-identical to before. The id is resolved inside the run's OWN tenant — naming another tenant's registration resolves to nothing — and an unknown, disabled or unwired target is DENIED, never run locally. The remote's reply is untrusted tool-result data and the folded child.result carries no child_run_id: no local run exists, and a remote task id is connection-scoped.

data.description: An offered engine checkpoint (spec §26.1-26.2, E10 Task 1). state is the OPAQUE loop-state bytes base64-encoded; the control plane stores and checksums them but never interprets them (§26.2). format/format_version pin compatibility against engine.ready.checkpoint_formats; boundary_kind records why the offer was made (completed tool, pause, explicit request).

state.description: base64 of the opaque checkpoint bytes

data.description: Restore a fresh engine process from a portable checkpoint (spec §26.3 rung 2, E10 Task 4) — the inbound mirror of checkpoint.offer. state is the OPAQUE loop-state bytes base64-encoded (the same bytes the control plane held); format/format_version must match engine.ready.checkpoint_formats or the engine answers protocol.error rather than half-restoring. The engine re-derives the frame it was awaiting at the captured boundary.

state.description: base64 of the opaque checkpoint bytes
